title: Predictive Score for feasibility of outpatient gynecologic surgery - evaluation of clinical value.
summary:
Development and validation of the clinical utility of a scoring system to ensure that outpatient surgery with discharge on the day of surgery (Same Day Discharge, SDD) is feasible. The score includes preoperative parameters of physical frailty and surgical planning, as well as postoperative parameters related to the surgical procedure.
Patient data will be evaluated prospectively. After completion of the study, the score may be implemented in preoperative and postoperative management if the study verifies its clinical utility. Patients who are not considered suitable for outpatient surgery will primarily undergo surgery in the hospital and receive postoperative inpatient care. For these patients, it cannot be determined whether outpatient surgery would have been possible. As a consequence of this preoperative triage, the prevalence of patients not discharged on the day of surgery is approximately 10%. Therefore, the study is primarily designed to provide a valid estimate of the positive predictive value of the SDD score. The negative predictive value will be analyzed exploratively. This approach is a direct consequence of the low prevalence. The study will therefore assess whether the SDD score achieves a positive predictive value of 95% (expected 95% confidence interval approximately ±3%), requiring data from 250 patients.
In addition, a postoperative survey will assess how many patients would choose SDD again. The survey will be conducted no earlier than 6 months after the procedure via questionnaire or telephone interview.
conditions: Patients with benign and malignant gynecologic conditions treated by operative laparoscopy, laparoscopic simple or radical hysterectomy, laparoscopic supracervical hysterectomy, laparoscopic adnexal surgery, laparoscopic pelvic and/or para-aortic lymphadenectomy with or without a sentinel node concept, partial or radical vulvectomy, inguinal lymphadenectomy with or without a sentinel node concept, laparoscopic pelvic floor reconstruction, or surgery for urinary incontinence.
